sources.title: RFC 3986: Uniform Resource Identifier Generic Syntax, section 2.3

claims.text: RFC 3986 defines letters and decimal digits as URI unreserved characters; the candidate's Base62 alphabet is a subset used as an unescaped path token.
The reproducible test verifies 62^5=916,132,832 and 62^6=56,800,235,584, proving that five Base62 characters do not cover the declared 10-billion assumption while six do.

The candidate explicitly presents range allocation, Base62 encoding, mapping uniqueness, idempotency, cache invalidation, multi-site write exclusion, and disaster recovery as a design proposal under declared assumptions, not as universal product behavior.

The reproducible state-model tests show non-overlapping sequential range claims, unused failed tails not being reissued, and repeated idempotency keys returning the first stored short code. The candidate makes production correctness conditional on an actual linearizable range-claim store and transactional uniqueness constraints.

findings: 需求假设缺少创建与解析延迟/SLO。
